Case reference: 2014003305.CaseDesc: On November 3, 1987, Wade Stanley Saxton was seen for the last time as he left his residence in St. Catharines, Ontario.

His family reported him missing on June 5, 2024, after they attended his residence and he wasn’t there.

Case reference: 2014004632.CaseDesc: On May 9th, 2005, Dean Phillips  was reported missing by his family in Campbell River, British Columbia. Dean was  last seen at a local school in Campbell River and has not been seen or heard from since.

Case reference: 2016069646.CaseDesc: James Kunuk was last seen by his family on September 21, 2016 and reported missing by his landlord in December, 2016 from Whitehorse, Yukon. James previously lived in downtown Vancouver, British Columbia and also has family connections to the Northwest Territories.  James did not contact his family for his birthday or over the Christmas holidays, which is unusual for him.

Tattoo: Left Forearm, Cross with "Life" written on it

Case reference: 2012020141.CaseDesc: On November 16, 1999, at approximately 9:00 p.m., Julie Surprenant was seen for the last time as she got off of a bus in the neighbourhood of L’Île St-Jean, in the suburb of Terrebone, in Montreal, Quebec. Case reference: 2014002167.CaseDesc: On July 7, 1973, William Gorrie and his family were seen by a an RCMP patrol boat returning from a day of fishing in Cross Bay, Manitoba. The waves increased in height and he followed the patrol boat, eventually getting his family on board. As a result, the patrol boat had to increase its power, significantly increasing the distance between the two boats. The last sighting of Mr. Gorrie's boat was approximately 1 km behind the patrol boat. An immediate search by air was conducted with negative results. It is presumed that William drowned as neither he nor the boat were ever located.

Case reference: 2012020011.CaseDesc: Daniel Richard McCallum was living in the Lillooet, BC area up until October 2008.  When his family hadn't heard from him for some time, they reported him missing. There are unconfirmed reports that he may have moved away, but police have been unable to determine his whereabouts. His disappearance is considered suspicious.

Case reference: 2012030001.CaseDesc: In April 2011, both parents took their son, Aleksander to visit the mother's family in Poland. The father came back to Canada on his own on May 13, 2011. The mother, Elzbieta Nowacki and child did not return to Canada.

Case reference: 2014001506.CaseDesc: During the early morning hours of February 24, 1991, Harrison Brown left a friend's home on snowmobile and was last seen traveling near open water.

Case reference: 2006010199.CaseDesc: Donald Chorney was last seen departing the Keys Lake Campground near Grassy Narrows, Ontario, to go for a boat ride.  He has not been seen since and is presumed to have drowned.

Case reference: 2024001775.CaseDesc: Brady Storey was reported missing to police by his mother on January 11, 2024 from Fredericton, New Brunswick. Frances Gazeley was last seen on the evening of December 7, 2021. She was last

Case reference: 2014004667.CaseDesc: On  November 25, 1999, the Gypsumville RCMP detachment received a report of an aircraft in distress over Lake Winnipeg near Reindeer Island, Manitoba. The aircraft, a single-engine Cherokee 140, was carrying three people; the pilot and two passengers. The pilot had declared that the engine had stalled and that he was trying to reach Reindeer Island. He then stated that he was going into the water. Two RCMP and an Air Search and Rescue Hercules aircrafts conducted an aerial search. It was not possible to search the lake by boat as there was too much ice on the lake. All three are presumed dead from drowning or the impact of the crash.

Case reference: 2014005673.CaseDesc: Tanya Nepinak was last seen leaving her home in downtown Winnipeg, Manitoba on September 13, 2011 to go shopping and has not been seen or heard from since. Tanya has always been in contact with her family and this behaviour is out of character for her.

Case reference: 2014004957.CaseDesc: On New Year's Eve, 2002 an anonymous letter was received by the Vancouver Police Department. The letter referred to a female Vancouver sex trade worker who had disappeared one month earlier, at the end of November. The letter writer described the woman, admitted to killing her, and apologized to her family for taking her life. Investigators believe the letter writer was referring to Danielle Marissa Larue, and while her body has never been found, they believe that she was murdered. The letter writer knows what happened to Danielle, and police are hopeful that the writer will contact them again.
